clearing_status.fact: SEC Press Release 2026-111 (sec.gov, Oct 30 2026): SEC issued exemptive relief (Release No. 34-106789) excluding certain inter-affiliate and non-U.S. repo transactions from the definition of eligible secondary market transactions. The operative compliance deadlines remain Dec 31 2026 (cash) and Jun 30 2027 (repo) under the single one-year extension (90 FR 11134, Feb 25 2025); no second deadline extension has been announced. The Oct 30 2026 relief is a targeted scope carve-out, not a deadline shift.
clearing_status.rationale: Rubric value 1 requires 'an official extension granted OR exemptive-relief requests pending.' The Feb 2025 one-year extension remains the operative framework, and the Oct 30 2026 formal exemptive relief order constitutes additional granted relief short of a full deadline extension — firmly satisfying value 1. No second formal deadline extension has been announced, so value 2 is not warranted.
clearing_status.change_reason: new_event: SEC granted formal exemptive relief (Release No. 34-106789, Oct 30 2026) for inter-affiliate and non-U.S. repo transactions, confirming ongoing SLIPPING dynamics but not escalating to a second deadline extension (value 2 threshold not met).

dc_moratoria.fact: electricchoice.com (Nov 4, 2026): '583 active restrictions across 46 states'; NY EO 62 (statewide moratorium, Jul 14, 2026) confirmed still in force as of Nov 2026 (llmpulse.ai Nov 15, sentisense.ai Nov 6); TX Gov. dc_moratoria.rationale: NY EO 62 alone satisfies the rubric's 'statewide moratorium enacted' threshold for value=2; the >10-jurisdiction criterion is independently satisfied by 583 confirmed enacted local restrictions across 46 states, further reinforced by Nov 3 midterm ballot approvals adding dozens more. No facts have changed since Nov 6 that would alter the classification.

dissent.view: Quorum (Oct 26, 2026) and ailawsbystate.com note no state legislature has enacted a moratorium by STATUTE; NY's action is executive-order-based and TX pauses are governor/agency directives, not passed legislation — a narrower reading that could argue the rubric's 'enacted' language requires statutory action.

ai_power_pressure.fact: ERCOT energization pause for data centers/crypto ≥75 MW remains in force as of 2026-11-14 (txdatacenterwatch.com, updated 2026-11-14); ~17 large loads (~6.6 GW) are blocked from energizing pending Dec 10 audit reports. Separately, ERCOT CEO Pablo Vegas confirmed on 2026-11-11 that 'ERCOT has not yet ordered data centers to curtail under SB6' (Insurance Journal / Bloomberg, 2026-11-12), and the ERCOT CEO is seeking NEW legislative authority to require earlier curtailment - a proposal not yet enacted.
ai_power_pressure.rationale: Interconnection queues remain blocked and projects are delayed for power by a governor-ordered moratorium (Rubric 1 criteria met). No forced curtailment of operating data-center load, no declared grid emergency, and no power-scarcity-driven moratorium on live facilities has been confirmed, so Rubric 2 is not met.

mine_disruptions.fact: Three or more top-20 copper mines confirmed with active output cuts as of mid-November 2026: (1) Grasberg/PTFI at ~67% capacity (249 Mlb in first 9 months of 2026, Tony Wenas, Minerba Convention, Nov 3 2026); (2) Kamoa-Kakula at ~290,000 t full-year 2026 vs ~500,000 t design, with Ivanhoe cutting 2027 guidance further to 300,000-350,000 t (Kamoa Capital Weekly Wrap, Nov 8 2026; Ivanhoe Q3 release, Oct 8 2026); (3) Codelco system: Andina processing halted by tailings spill (Nov 5-6 2026, Northern Miner) and 2026 guidance cut to ~1.2 Mt vs 1.34 Mt target (Reuters/Codelco shareholder meeting, Nov 5 2026); Cochilco cut Chile national 2026 forecast 8.4% to 4.94 Mt; Goldman projects 950,000 t refined copper deficit ex-US in 2026 (discoveryalert.com, Nov 2026).
mine_disruptions.rationale: Four distinct major copper operations (Grasberg, Kamoa-Kakula, Codelco-Andina, and broader Codelco/Escondida/Spence complex) have confirmed active production cuts or outages, well exceeding the >=3 mine threshold; Goldman and Cochilco both explicitly forecast a copper market deficit, satisfying either CLUSTER criterion independently.
mine_disruptions.change_reason: new_event: Post-Nov-3 developments include Ivanhoe cutting 2027 Kamoa-Kakula guidance to 300,000-350,000 t (Nov 8 2026), Codelco confirming Andina tailings spill halting processing and cutting 2026 guidance to ~1.2 Mt (Nov 5-6 2026), and Cochilco cutting Chile national forecast 8.4% (Nov 5 2026) — these reinforce and extend the CLUSTER reading with additional mines and institutional deficit forecasts.

dissent.view: Codelco output scandal (42,100 t) reflects historical misreporting of 2024-2025 figures, not a new physical outage; actual 2026 physical output decline is structural/gradual rather than a discrete disruption event

copper_deficit_timing.fact: ICSG biannual forecast issued 14-15 October 2026: global refined copper market surplus of ~104,000 metric tons in 2026, widening to ~368,000 mt in 2027. Source: Mining Weekly, 15 Oct 2026; confirmed by IndexBox, The Oregon Group, and discoveryalert.com (Nov 2026).
copper_deficit_timing.rationale: The ICSG October 2026 forecast is unambiguously a surplus of 104,000 mt for 2026, well above zero and in positive territory; under the rubric, any official surplus forecast maps directly to value=0 (SURPLUS). No post-Oct-15 data or event revises this finding.

drought_chip_farm.fact: USDM National Drought Summary (droughtmonitor.unl.edu, data valid Nov 10 2026, released Nov 12 2026): 'prolific rainfall continued in parts of the Southwest... leading to significant drought improvement'; Desert Southwest reservoirs filling 'at an exceptionally rapid pace' — Navajo Reservoir at 110% of average seasonal storage, Lake Powell +1.4M acre-feet since mid-September. No D3/D4 for Southwest. Taiwan reservoirs.earth (WRA data, Oct 22 2026): 22 tracked reservoirs average 59.2% full, 'within normal operating range', 0 of 22 in drought zone. No rationing order in force in either region.
drought_chip_farm.rationale: Southwest drought is improving broadly with no D2+ conditions persisting at key farm/fab hubs, and Taiwan reservoirs are near-normal with no rationing order; neither region meets the rubric threshold for a rating above 0. No new event since Nov 3 changes the outcome.

reservoir_stress.fact: Lake Mead elevation 1,041.14 ft, storage 7,051,516 acre-feet, ~27% of USBR active capacity (26,120,000 AF basis) as of Nov 15, 2026 — 3rd-lowest for that calendar date in 92 years of Reclamation record. Source: USBR RISE API via lakelevelnow.com (Nov 15, 2026).
reservoir_stress.rationale: At ~27% of USBR active capacity, Lake Mead remains below the 30% CRITICAL threshold, satisfying rubric band 2 independently of the power-pool proximity test. The reservoir has risen ~1.6 ft since Nov 7 but no event has pushed storage above 30%, so the rubric outcome is unchanged.

dissent.view: lakelevelnow.com reports 24% full using total pool capacity basis (~36.7M AF at 1,229 ft full pool) rather than USBR active capacity (26.12M AF); both yield <30% so rubric outcome is identical.

water_dispute.fact: Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif declared on 21 Oct 2026 that any IWT violation 'will be treated as an act of war'; Pakistan Senate Chairman Gillani reiterated the identical formulation at Pakistan Water Week on 2 Nov 2026; India's IWT abeyance remains in force and India has rejected the PCA's 31 Aug 2026 ruling that the treaty is fully binding (Pakistan Today, 21 Oct 2026; Nation.com.pk, 13 Nov 2026; PCA press release, 31 Aug 2026; Al Jazeera, 1 Sep 2026).
water_dispute.rationale: An explicit threat of war tied to a river, made by a head of government (PM Sharif, 21 Oct 2026) and reiterated by the Senate Chairman (Gillani, 2 Nov 2026) — both within the 90-day window — satisfies the rubric's Level 2 criterion. No new armed clash or deliberate cut-off has occurred, but the qualifying ministerial war threat is current and unretracted.

dissent.view: Analysts note India's existing infrastructure cannot yet physically cut off Pakistan's water, and characterise the dispute as 'strategic securitisation' rather than imminent war (Global Defense Corp, 9 Nov 2026)

fao_food_trend.fact: FAO Food Price Index averaged 133.9 points in October 2026, down 1.6 points (1.2%) MoM from revised September level of 136.0, but still 5.9% above year-earlier level. Source: FAO newsroom, released 6 November 2026 (fao.org/newsroom/detail/fao-food-price-index-edges-down-in-october-amid-subdued-demand/en). Next release covering November 2026 data is scheduled 4 December 2026 and has not yet been published.
fao_food_trend.rationale: MoM decline of 1.2% rules out rubric band 0 (index is not down YoY; +5.9% YoY keeps it elevated). MoM change of 1.2% is below both the 3% threshold for band 1 ceiling and the 5% spike threshold, and the 3-month cumulative rise does not reach 10%, so band 2 is not triggered; band 1 applies.

china_export_curbs.fact: Prosperous America (Nov 10, 2026) reports China phosphate export restrictions remain in place: September 2026 customs data show zero DAP and zero agricultural MAP exports; Argus now forecasts no phosphate export restart until May 2027; urea quota locked at 3.3 Mt (34% below 2025 actuals) with FOB price floors of $430-440/t (Fertilizer Daily, Sep 18 2026). MOFCOM Oct 29 2026 2027-quota release confirms phosphate rock export quota suspension continues under licensing-only regime.
china_export_curbs.rationale: The phosphate suspension — originally through Aug 31 2026 — was not lifted; zero DAP/MAP cleared customs in September and Argus forecasts resumption only in May 2027, confirming the suspension has been extended de facto into 2027, a tightening first captured pre-Nov 3 that remains in force. Urea remains under a tightened quota 34% below prior-year actuals with price floors, satisfying rubric band 2 (new/broadened restriction confirmed with physical shipment impact).

dissent.view: SMM/Keyuan (Sep 1 2026) reported China 'resumed normal export declarations for agricultural phosphate fertilisers' from Sep 1, suggesting temporary suspension lifted — but subsequent September customs data and S&P Global/Argus reporting confirm no actual DAP/MAP shipments occurred, making this an administrative formality not a physical resumption.

hormuz_fertilizer.fact: IMF PortWatch recorded 3 commercial transits on November 8, 2026 (latest published day), with a 7-day average of 3.9/day — 4% of the pre-crisis baseline of ~87/day. Source: straits.live live tracker updated 16 NOV 2026 0124Z and hormuz.now FAQ updated 16 NOV 2026 04:01 UTC, both sourcing portwatch.imf.org.
hormuz_fertilizer.rationale: A 7-day IMF PortWatch average of 3.9 transits/day is ~4% of the ~87/day baseline, well below the 25% threshold; the rubric mandates 2=CUT for transits below 25% of baseline, which is confirmed with no ambiguity. Gulf fertilizer, sulfur and ammonia loadings through Hormuz are correspondingly near-zero given this near-total blockade.

dissent.view: UANI (United Against Nuclear Iran) reports U.S.-facilitated transits averaged 33.8 vessels/day (Nov 8–11, 2026), suggesting partial escorted throughput not captured by IMF PortWatch AIS counts
TankerMap AIS data shows ~21 tanker transits/day as of mid-November 2026, counting vessels including those with intermittent AIS

taiwan_tension.fact: Taiwan MND (Nov. 14, 2026): 10 PLA aircraft sorties, 8 PLAN vessels, 3 official ships detected; 4 sorties crossed the median line into central/SW/eastern ADIZ. Month-to-date: 184 aircraft and 141 ship detections. France24 (Nov. 13) and Taipei Times (Nov. 14) confirm no actual blockade — PLA conducted large unannounced drills simulating Taiwan isolation in early November ('silent intimidation'), now subsiding to elevated but lower daily figures. No kinetic clash or formal blockade implemented. Sources: Taiwan MND via Taiwan News (Nov. 14); France24 (Nov. 13); Taipei Times (Nov. 14); Focus Taiwan CNA (Nov. 14).
taiwan_tension.rationale: Activity meets Rubric 1: large-scale PLA drills and blockade rehearsals (ISW/AEI-assessed unannounced isolation exercise, multi-theater force deployment, CCG confrontations) with no kinetic clash or actual blockade confirmed; daily sorties declining from Nov. 2 peak but remain assertively elevated above routine baseline. [cross-check (asi1): two reads disagreed (1 vs 0); held for review]

dissent.view: Pacific Strategic Intelligence Weekly (Nov. 15) characterizes continuing operations as 'area denial' drills with Liaoning carrier group extended at sea, suggesting the exercise posture has not fully concluded and may warrant closer monitoring for escalation.

export_controls.fact: China MOFCOM Announcement No. 48 (Oct 16, 2026) placed 40 AI/chip/solar technologies under immediately effective interim export-registration requirements; public comment closed Nov 15, 2026 and MOFCOM is now finalizing the catalogue (Jones Day, Nov 2026; Lexology; Baker McKenzie). China's Jul 24 2026 Announcement No. 30 (14 EU entities on Export Control List) remains in force. On Nov 13, 2026 China's Foreign Ministry publicly warned the US against new chip export controls (CBS News/AFP, Nov 13 2026). On the allied side, the MATCH Act (would ban DUV immersion exports to China) remains pending in Congress as of Nov 5, 2026 (Startup Fortune, Nov 5 2026; CSIS), and House Speaker Johnson signaled growing congressional consensus for tighter controls (CBS News, Nov 13 2026).
export_controls.rationale: Both rubric conditions for level 2 are met: (1) US/allied tightening measures are ongoing — NL/EU controls in force, MATCH Act pending, congressional pressure intensifying; (2) China has enacted countermeasures — Announcement 48 interim registration in force since Oct 16 and moving to finalization, Jul 2026 EU entity list additions still active. No new enacted measure post-Nov 9 changes the rubric outcome; China's Nov 13 warning is diplomatic, not a new enacted control, and the rare-earth waiver extension is de-escalatory on that sub-front.

dissent.view: Rare-earth waiver extended to Jan 10, 2027 (Reuters/US News, Nov 9 2026) and analysts note US-China trade talks 'remain on track' ahead of planned Trump-Xi APEC meeting — suggesting partial de-escalation on that specific sub-front that could argue for capping at 1

fab_concentration.fact: TSMC 3nm capacity ~180,000+ wpm (all Taiwan fabs) and 2nm capacity ~90,000-100,000 wpm (all five Taiwan fabs: 2 Hsinchu + 3 Kaohsiung) as of Q4 2026. Arizona Fab 21 Phase 2 (N3): equipment installation ongoing since Q3 2026, volume production targeted H2 2027 — zero <=3nm wafers produced outside Taiwan. Japan JASM Fab 2 (3nm): HVM 2028. 0% of <=3nm capacity is outside Taiwan today. Sources: TSMC Q3 2026 earnings (Oct 15 2026); VentureAtlas Nov 2026; TrendForce/Economic Daily News (Aug 2026); tech-insider.org (Oct 2026).
fab_concentration.rationale: 0% of <=3nm capacity sits outside Taiwan as of mid-November 2026 — well below the rubric's 10% threshold — and no overseas fab is producing leading-edge wafers, satisfying both conditions for EXTREME (value=2). Arizona Fab 21 Phase 2 tool install is underway but volume production is not expected until H2 2027, so no rubric threshold has been crossed.

hormuz_redsea_status.fact: IMF PortWatch recorded 3 commercial transits through the Strait of Hormuz on 8 November 2026 (latest published day; 7-day average 3.9/day), against a pre-crisis baseline of ~85/day = 4% of baseline. Corroborated by straits.live Nov 16 brief and worldmonitor.app Nov 14. IRGC mine/fire incidents on a gas carrier and multiple tankers reported Nov 13-16 (straits.live Nov 16 brief). Bab el-Mandeb: Lloyd's List Intelligence Nov 12 brief reports 1,363 transits in October (~44/day vs ~70/day baseline, ~63%); no attacks since Aug 24 (UKMTO via Lloyd's). Hormuz is worse chokepoint.
hormuz_redsea_status.rationale: Hormuz at 4% of baseline is far below the 25% CLOSED threshold, satisfying rubric level 2 for the worse of the two chokepoints. Ongoing mine strikes and tanker attacks through 13-16 November further confirm active interdiction, reinforcing CLOSED status with no change from the prior reading.

dissent.view: UANI (Nov 13 2026) reports 33.8 US-facilitated transits/day (Nov 8-11), suggesting partial reopening via southern corridor; however these are dark AIS transits under US Navy escort not captured by IMF PortWatch, and the rubric anchors to measured PortWatch counts

Wikipedia 2026 Hormuz crisis article cites oil flows at ~82% of pre-war via offshore/pipeline transfers; this is a volume/bypass metric, not vessel transit count, and does not override AIS-measured transits per rubric

cable_incidents.fact: As of Nov 13, 2026 (Brinztech/Reuters), Iran has drawn up contingency plans to cut Hormuz cables if hostilities resume, IRGC Brig. Gen. Mohebbi publicly threatened all seven Hormuz cables on Oct 19 and Javani on Oct 21, and Windward (Oct 29) flagged four Iran-linked vessels loitering AIS-dark over Hormuz cable corridors — but 'no cable has been cut' (shiftdelete.net, Nov 7, 2026). Sept 2025 Red Sea cuts (SMW4, IMEWE, FALCON GCX) are confirmed repaired per prior APNIC Oct 14, 2026 sourcing. No new cut is confirmed in any corridor post-Nov 9, 2026.
cable_incidents.rationale: Rubric 1 (THREATENED) is met by credible IRGC public threats (Oct 19-21, 2026, within 90 days) and anomalous vessel behavior over cable corridors (Oct 2026); rubric 2 (CUT) is not met because no authoritative source confirms an active, unrepaired cable severance today, and no connectivity or price signal corroborates a cut.

dissent.view: Rest of World and Capacity Global describe both Red Sea and Hormuz as 'effectively closed to commercial traffic' and repair vessels unable to operate, implying cables are at acute functional risk — but neither confirms a physical cable cut post-Sept 2025.

rb.ax blog states 'Both the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea are now effectively closed to commercial cable repair vessels' (citing Submarine Networks, Mar 2026) — characterising the repair access denial as equivalent to a cut, but this is a functional assessment from March 2026, not a confirmed post-Nov 9 severance.

treasury_clearing_rollout.fact: FICC/DTCC survey (July 27, 2026) shows 79% of GSD Netting Members already have account setups; nearly 100% are onboarded or in pipeline; $1.2T+ already clearing daily with ~$300-400B still to migrate. SEC issued two targeted exemptive relief orders post-Nov 4: Oct 30 (Release No. 34-106789, non-US/inter-affiliate repo) and Nov 4 (Release No. 34-106821, broker-dealer Note H relief). Cash deadline Dec 31, 2026 and repo deadline Jun 30, 2027 remain unchanged. SIFMA/BNY/Broadridge/DTCC pulse survey (June 2026, n=340, pub. Sept 22 2026) shows 45% still need regulatory clarity and 51% have no formal contingency plan. Sources: dtcc.com July 27 2026; sec.gov Oct 30 and Nov 4 2026; sifma.org Sept 22 2026.
treasury_clearing_rollout.rationale: No deadline extension or major operational failure has occurred, ruling out level 2. However, continued exemptive relief issuance (two orders in 15 days), 45% of firms lacking regulatory clarity, 51% with no contingency plan, and meaningful repo documentation work outstanding all meet the rubric definition of FRICTION (pending exemptive relief, readiness gaps). Cash is trending toward resolution but repo work-remaining is substantive.

dissent.view: FICC GSD member survey (July 2026) shows ~79% already set up for cash clearing and near-100% in onboarding pipeline, suggesting cash readiness is closer to SMOOTH than FRICTION for direct participants
Glenn Handley (SecFin Solutions, May 2026 Substack) argues infrastructure is not ready despite fixed deadlines, implying risk of level 2

oat_bund.fact: ideal-investisseur.fr (citing Banque de France & Deutsche Bundesbank data), Nov 16 2026: OAT-Bund 10-year spread = 155.0 bps (OAT 4.93%, Bund 3.38%), up 3.2 bps from prior session. Corroborated by Milano Finanza (Nov 16 2026, 17:15 CET) quoting the OAT/Bund spread at 157 bps intraday (OAT 4.94%, Bund ~3.37%).
oat_bund.rationale: 155.0 bps (ideal-investisseur end-of-day, Banque de France/Bundesbank sourced) = 1.55 percentage points, materially above the last reading of 1.48 on 2026-11-05; the spread has widened ~7 bps on the week, driven by continued French fiscal/political uncertainty ahead of the 2027 budget. Rubric maps this directly: 155.0 bps = 1.55 in percentage-point units.
oat_bund.change_reason: new_event: OAT-Bund spread widened to 155.0 bps by Nov 16 2026 (from 148 bps on Nov 5), reflecting continued French fiscal pressure and OAT selloff resumption after a brief relief rally around Nov 9-10

dissent.view: Milano Finanza (Nov 16 2026, 17:15 CET) quoted OAT/Bund spread at 157 bps intraday (OAT 4.94%, Bund ~3.37%) — slightly wider than ideal-investisseur end-of-day 155.0 bps, likely reflecting intraday vs. closing price difference
cbonds.com data as of Nov 10 2026 showed 10Y France-Germany spread at 148.4 bps — consistent with the brief post-Moody's relief rally, now superseded by today's wider reading
